trust_decision.summary: Decided at the /debug/vrlog HTTP handler: the handler is registered on the bare servenv mux with no acl.CheckAccessHTTP call, so any client that can reach the vttablet HTTP port is served a live stream of the SQL the vplayer applies and of the source row values; the only gate is the startup flag --vreplication-enable-http-log (default false), copied into each workflow's VReplicationConfig and tested by the vplayer before each emission. The published fix does not add a check: it deletes the handler, the emission sites, the config field and demotes the flag to an accepted no-op, i.e. the trust decision becomes 'the endpoint does not exist'. Note that the project's own ACL default is allow-all (empty --security-policy), so a CheckAccessHTTP-only fix is a no-op unless the operator configures a policy.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only 'missing authorization on vttablet /debug/vrlog' greps the route path and lands on the servenv.HTTPHandleFunc registration; the handler, the streamlog subscriber and the record shape (Type/Detail template at vrlog.go:38-39) are all in that one 126-line file.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The endpoint is an internal, undocumented feature that is off by default and was explicitly documented as disabled by default since v22 (changelog/22.0/22.0.0/changelog.md:485), so a solver can argue the exposure only exists in a deployment that opted in, and that the flag/defaults loader in go/vt/vttablet/common is startup plumbing rather than part of the advisory's /debug/vrlog scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: vttablet and vtcombo must keep accepting --vreplication-enable-http-log on the command line as a deprecated no-op so existing startup scripts do not fail to start, while the flag must disappear from --help (pflag hides deprecated flags); the golden help file go/flags/endtoend/vttablet.txt:430 still lists the flag at the pinned commit and is compared by TestHelpOutput (go/flags/endtoend/flags_test.go:115). Deleting the flag registration breaks the first requirement; leaving it a visible BoolVar breaks the second.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an emitter for the batch/atomic row-change path that logs the generated bulk INSERT/DELETE SQL directly to the same streamlog without the EnableHttpLog gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the parent commit added a parallel bulk path that runs through the same applyFunc (vplayer.go:401-411) and has its own query flow; a maintainer adding log coverage for batch mode would naturally add a second emission site there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a vdiff-side emitter pushing diff query SQL into the same /debug/vrlog stream
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a vestigial LogExpectation type is still declared in the vdiff test framework, showing the vdiff package once consumed the vrlog logger; extending the same log to vdiff query SQL is a plausible maintainer change in a neighbouring workflow.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a /debug/vstream endpoint streaming vstreamer event SQL, registered on the servenv mux without an ACL check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the vstreamer engine already registers a debug HTTP handler in the same init (tablet_vschema) and vrlog.go:71-77 is the exact template for a second unguarded streaming handler, so a sibling written by the same maintainers is realistic.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add acl.CheckAccessHTTP(r, acl.DEBUGGING) at the top of the /debug/vrlog handler (copying txlogz.go:79) and leave the flag, the config field and the vplayer emission sites in place - it verifies green under --security-policy=deny-all, but the default empty policy keeps streaming every replicated SQL statement and row value.
